blockers.message: the review record has no `## code.review` section, while roles were active at it
R-accessibility-1 (Field errors are conveyed by a red border only, with no text message) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
`field--invalid`, a red border (`#e5484d`); the list of errors at the top of
the page is removed, since the red border already shows where the problem
is. No message text is added, to keep the form compact.
findings.recommendation: Show the rule's message (rules.ts already returns "Enter a 5-digit postcode, such as 75011.") in text under each invalid field, associate it with `aria-describedby`, and set `aria-invalid="true"` on the input — WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color, 3.3.1 Error Identification, 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value. Today a screen reader user who leaves the postcode field with `ABC` hears nothing (only a CSS class changes), and a colour-blind user sees no difference from the grey border; nobody learns what the expected format is. Update the spec scenario "An invalid postcode" (THEN only "the field's border turns red") and task 1.2 so they require the message and its association, not only the border colour.
findings.title: Field errors are conveyed by a red border only, with no text message

findings.evidence: - The error list at the top of the form is removed.
findings.recommendation: The removed summary is the form's only `role="alert"` (Form.tsx:22), so after the change a keyboard or screen reader user who presses Pay with an invalid or never-visited field gets no announcement and no focus change — the submit silently does nothing (WCAG 3.3.1 Error Identification, 2.4.3 Focus Order). State in the design what happens on submit: validate every field, then move focus to the first invalid field (or keep a focusable error summary with links to the fields), and add a scenario for it in the spec.
findings.title: Submitting an invalid form is no longer announced and focus is not moved
